items.text: Explain how DNS resolves a domain name — name all 4 server types in order
Describe what TTL is and why it matters for DNS updates
Explain the difference between a domain registrar and an authoritative nameserver
Describe what a hosted zone is and the difference between public and private hosted zones
Name and describe at least 5 DNS record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SOA)
Explain Route 53 Alias records and when to use them instead of CNAME
Purchase a domain name in Route 53 or GoDaddy
Create a public hosted zone in Route 53 for a domain
Create an A record with Alias pointing to a CloudFront distribution
Update GoDaddy name servers with Route 53 NS values (link GoDaddy + Route 53)
Set up a private S3 bucket with CloudFront + OAC for a static website
Configure a Route 53 weighted routing policy for A/B testing
Draw the full S3 → CloudFront (OAC) → ACM → Route 53 → User architecture from memory
Trace the traffic flow for a first-time user request vs. a repeat request (caching layers)
Explain why a CNAME cannot be used at the zone apex and what to use instead
Identify the correct routing policy for latency, failover, A/B testing, and geo-compliance scenarios
State that ACM certificates for CloudFront must be created in us-east-1
Know that Route 53 is the only AWS service with a 100% availability SLA
Recall that Route 53 generates exactly 4 NS records per hosted zone
Distinguish between OAC (new) and OAI (old deprecated method) for CloudFront + S3 access
